🧲🤯 Scientists Confirm a Third Type of Magnetism! ⚛️✨

We all know that magnets can attract or repel each other. But did you know that scientists have now confirmed a fascinating new form of magnetism? 🔬

Researchers at Stanford University and SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, USA, have provided strong experimental evidence for a third type of magnetic order called altermagnetism.

Their findings were published in the prestigious journal Science in October 2026. 📖

🔬 What did scientists discover?

For decades, scientists studied two major types of magnetic order in materials.

🧲 Ferromagnetism: Tiny magnetic moments inside a material align in the same direction. This produces the familiar magnetism we see in refrigerator magnets.

⚛️ Antiferromagnetism: Neighboring magnetic moments point in opposite directions. Their effects cancel, producing no overall magnetization.

But altermagnetism is different!

In these materials, magnetic moments also point in opposite directions. However, the arrangement of atoms creates unusual electronic properties.

The researchers studied a material called manganese telluride (MnTe).

Using powerful X-rays, they detected a special magnetic signature that provides strong evidence for altermagnetism. 🤯

💡 Why is this important?

Modern computers use electrical charges to process and store information.

But scientists are exploring another possibility: using a property of electrons called spin.

This technology is known as spintronics. 💻⚡

Altermagnetic materials could offer exciting advantages.

They may combine the stability of antiferromagnets with useful electronic properties associated with ferromagnets.

This could eventually help engineers develop faster and more energy-efficient electronic devices.

🌍 And here is the exciting part!

Imagine future computers that use less electricity while processing enormous amounts of information! 🤖

Such advances could become especially important as AI systems and data centers demand more computing power.

Practical applications still require substantial research. But confirming this new magnetic order is an important step toward understanding and controlling these materials.

Sometimes, a discovery about something as familiar as magnetism can open entirely new possibilities for future technology! 🚀✨

text:
Good morning from Virginia. 🇺🇸

On the last day of October 1776, King George III rode through the streets of London to open Parliament. He came in the full ceremony of the Crown, cloaked in ermine, to address both Houses on the one subject that now dominated the mind of the kingdom: the war in America. Nearly four months had passed since the Continental Congress had declared the colonies free and independent. The news had reached London in August. The king could no longer pretend the rupture was temporary or the product of a few hotheads in Massachusetts.

He began with the sentence he most wished he did not have to speak. Nothing, he told the assembled lords and commoners, could have given him greater satisfaction than to announce that the troubles which had so long distracted his colonies were at an end, that his “unhappy people” had recovered from their delusion and returned to their duty. Instead he faced a different reality. “So daring and desperate is the spirit of those leaders,” he declared, “whose object has always been dominion and power, that they have now openly renounced all allegiance to the Crown, and all political connection with this country.” They had rejected every offer of conciliation “with circumstances of indignity and insult,” and had “presumed to set up their rebellious confederacies for independent states.”

If that treason were suffered to take root, he warned, the consequences would reach far beyond America—to the safety of his loyal colonies, to the commerce of his kingdoms, and to the present system of all Europe. Yet he found one advantage in the rebels’ open avowal of their goal. Britain would now have “unanimity at home, founded in the general conviction of the justice and necessity of our measures.”

He spoke next of the military picture. By the blessing of Providence, Canada had been recovered. The operations at New York, delayed until August, had produced important success—the victory at Long Island, the capture of the city—and gave “the strongest hopes of the most decisive good consequences.” But the king would not claim the war was won. “Notwithstanding this fair prospect,” he said, “we must, at all events, prepare for another campaign.” In this “arduous conflict,” he insisted, he could have no object but the true interests of all his subjects. “No people ever enjoyed more happiness, or lived under a milder government, than those now revolted provinces.”

Across the Atlantic the picture looked different. Washington’s army had been driven from Long Island and from New York. It was short of men, short of powder, short of shoes. Many enlistments would expire at the end of the year. The Howe brothers still hoped that a show of British strength, combined with an offer of pardon, might bring the colonies back into the empire. The king’s speech left little room for that hope. When copies of the address finally reached American printers in the winter and early spring of 1777, they were read as a final confirmation that Britain intended to crush the rebellion by force.

The king had correctly judged that the American leaders would not return to the old order. What he could not yet see was the quality of the men and the idea they had set in motion. Within weeks Washington would cross the Delaware in a winter storm and strike at Trenton. Within a year the victory at Saratoga would bring France into the war. The campaign George III said Britain must prepare for would stretch on through years of hardship, foreign alliances, and the eventual surrender at Yorktown. The “rebellious confederacies” he dismissed would become the United States.

On that October day in Westminster the outcome was still uncertain. The king spoke with the confidence of a monarch who believed the resources of Britain and the justice of his cause would prevail. History would soon test both assumptions.

Why Support Independent Authors: Stories Matter
A book can begin with a muddy paw print, a half-heard remark at the local diner, or a question that will not stop scratching at an author’s mind. That is one reason why support independent authors: readers do more than buy a story. They help make room for the unusual, heartfelt, funny, and deeply personal books that might never fit neatly on a big publisher’s shelf.

For readers who love a clever small-town mystery, a dog with opinions, a cat who knows more than it lets on, or a children’s story with genuine warmth, independent books offer a very happy hunting ground. They are often written close to the author’s own passions, professions, communities, and sense of humor. The result can feel less like a product selected by committee and more like an invitation from a storyteller who has saved you a seat on the porch.

## Why Support Independent Authors? It Keeps More Stories Possible

Traditional publishing serves an important purpose, but it must make choices based on limited schedules, sales expectations, and broad market trends. A publishing house may love a manuscript yet decide it is too specific, too cross-genre, or simply not the kind of book its current list can carry. Independent authors can take a different path.

They can write the cozy mystery with a retired veterinarian, animal patients, historical Florida details, and canine forensics. They can create a gentle children’s book because they believe young readers need it. They can continue a series after a publisher might have moved on, giving loyal readers more time with favorite characters and familiar streets.

That freedom does not mean every independent book will suit every reader. Tastes are wonderfully particular. One person wants a fast-paced puzzle with suspects on every page; another wants a slower mystery with a cup of tea, a rescued animal, and neighbors who feel like old friends. Supporting independent authors means supporting the chance for both kinds of books to exist.

## Independent Books Carry a Personal Signature

Many readers can recognize when an author has written from a place of real curiosity. Perhaps it is the way a character handles an anxious dog, the details of a coastal storm, or the affectionate teasing between friends who have known one another for years. Those details are not always flashy, but they give a story its heartbeat.

Independent authors often have more room to follow that heartbeat. They may write outside the hottest trend because they know their readers are looking for something else. They may choose a cover style that suits the series rather than a passing fashion. They may publish at a pace that works for the story and their real life, whether that means releasing several books a year or taking the time needed to get the clues just right.

For cozy mystery readers, this can be especially rewarding. A good cozy series depends on trust. Readers want fair clues, characters worth revisiting, a setting that feels welcoming, and enough surprises to keep the whiskers twitching. Independent authors can nurture those elements book by book, listening closely to what readers respond to while keeping the series true to its own personality.

### The details are often the delight

A book does not need a world-saving quest to matter. Sometimes the delight is in a local festival, a stubborn beagle, a historic home with a troublesome past, or a sleuth who notices what everyone else overlooks. Independent authors are often willing to spend time in those smaller moments because they understand that readers come back for more than the answer to the mystery.

They come back for companionship. They want to know whether the bakery is still open, whether the cranky neighbor has softened, and whether the dog has learned absolutely nothing from last time. A series can become a place to visit when the real world feels a little too noisy.

## Your Support Reaches Far Beyond One Sale

Buying a book matters, of course. Independent authors pay editors, cover designers, formatters, illustrators, and sometimes narrators from the income their books earn. A purchase can help fund the next installment, the next revision, or the next bright idea scribbled down before breakfast.

But support is not limited to purchasing every book an author writes. A thoughtful review, a recommendation to a friend, a request at a local library, or a kind note after finishing a story can have real weight. Readers are often the best detectives when it comes to helping a good book find its next audience.

Reviews are especially useful because they help hesitant readers decide whether a book is right for them. The most helpful review does not need to be long or polished. A few honest sentences about what you enjoyed can do the job. Did the mystery keep you guessing? Did the animal characters make you smile? Did the small-town setting feel like a place you would gladly visit? Those specifics help another reader follow the trail.

Word of mouth also protects the joy of reading from becoming too narrow. When people only encounter books backed by the largest advertising budgets, many wonderful voices remain harder to find. Recommending an independent author is a small act of literary neighborliness. You are saying, in effect, “I found something good. Come see.”

## Supporting Authors Builds a Friendlier Reading Community

There is something special about knowing the person behind the book is reachable. Independent authors may answer a reader’s message, share a glimpse of research, celebrate a bookstore event, or laugh along when someone points out that the dog is clearly the wisest character in the room. That connection should always be respectful, since authors need quiet time to write and ordinary life to remain ordinary. Still, it can make reading feel less lonely.

A healthy reading community is not built on constant purchasing or endless online chatter. It is built on generosity. Readers share books, librarians champion new voices, book clubs trade theories, and authors keep creating because someone showed up for the last story. The chain is simple, but it is powerful.

For animal lovers, that community can be particularly warm. A reader who comes for a canine narrator may also find a new appreciation for animal welfare, veterinary work, training, or the strange and lovely bond between people and their pets. Fiction cannot replace professional advice, but it can encourage empathy. A story told with a warm snout and a sharp eye can remind us to pay attention to the creatures sharing our homes and lives.

## What Thoughtful Support Looks Like

The best support is the kind that feels natural rather than forced. Read what genuinely interests you. If you enjoy it, tell someone who might enjoy it too. Leave an honest review without spoilers. Ask your library whether it can add the title. Bring an independent author’s book to a club meeting when it fits the group’s taste.

It also helps to be patient with the realities of small publishing. Independent authors manage many jobs that a large publishing team might divide among several people. They may be writing, revising, arranging cover art, handling newsletters, planning events, and trying to remember where they left the good pen. Delays happen. Series may shift direction. A favorite character may not appear in every book. These are not always signs of trouble. Often, they are signs that a real person is carefully building a body of work.

At the same time, readers deserve books that have been treated with care. Supporting independent authors does not require pretending every book is perfect. Honest feedback, offered kindly, can be valuable. Choose the stories you enjoy, celebrate the work that earns your enthusiasm, and let your own reading life lead the way.

The next time you finish a book that made you grin, suspect the wrong neighbor, or look more fondly at the dog curled up beside your chair, pause before you move on to the next clue. A few words shared with another reader may help that author write the story you will be glad to find later.

THE BOY WHOSE HAND-DRAWN SHIRT HELPED RAISE NEARLY $1 MILLION

September 2019 — Florida, USA

A fourth-grade boy wanted to show his love for the University of Tennessee. He didn’t have an official shirt, so he did something simple and creative: he made his own.

He had no idea that a piece of paper, an orange T-shirt, and a hand-drawn logo would soon inspire thousands of people.

 A Homemade Shirt, A Hurtful Moment

During College Colors Day at Altamonte Elementary School in Altamonte Springs, Florida, the young student proudly wore an orange shirt with his homemade University of Tennessee “UT” design pinned to the front.

He was excited to represent the college he admired.

But after lunch, some classmates made fun of his creation. According to his teacher, Laura Snyder, he returned to the classroom crying and devastated.

For a child who had simply wanted to participate and show his school spirit, the experience was deeply upsetting.

A Teacher’s Post Changed Everything

Snyder shared what happened on Facebook. She hoped to find a way to get her student an official University of Tennessee shirt and make him feel better.

Her post quickly spread among Tennessee fans, eventually reaching the university.

The response was remarkable.

The university sent a package filled with official merchandise for the boy and his classmates. But the support didn’t end there.

The university’s official store decided to turn the boy’s original, hand-drawn design into a real T-shirt that fans could purchase.

Something that had been mocked at school was now being celebrated by people across the country.

 More Than 112,000 Shirts Sold

The response was extraordinary.

By December 2019, 112,715 shirts had been sold, raising $952,101 for STOMP Out Bullying, a nonprofit organization dedicated to preventing bullying.

Thousands of people were now wearing a design that had started with one young fan’s simple attempt to show his school spirit.

And the university had another surprise.

 A Scholarship for the Future

In September 2019, the University of Tennessee offered the boy honorary admission to its Class of 2032 and a four-year scholarship covering tuition and fees, beginning in fall 2028—provided he chose to attend and met the university’s admission requirements.

It was an extraordinary gesture for a child whose handmade shirt had sparked such a powerful response.

 A Lesson Bigger Than a T-Shirt

This story is a reminder that a small act of kindness can change how a child sees the world.

The boy’s drawing didn’t need to be perfect. He didn’t need an expensive shirt to prove his enthusiasm. He simply wanted to belong.

When others chose to laugh, his teacher chose to speak up—and a university community chose to respond with kindness.

A design that began as a child’s homemade logo became a symbol of something much bigger: the importance of standing up against bullying and helping children feel valued.

Sometimes, the most meaningful thing we can do is make sure a child never feels ashamed of being himself.

text:
Pillar I: The Intended Message (Textual & Historical Context)
Chapters 19 through 21 of 2 Samuel document the precarious restoration of David’s monarchy, the lingering consequences of internal fracture, and the inescapable demands of divine justice. Rather than depicting an idealized, triumphant return, the narrative records the grinding political and spiritual fallout of the rebellion of Absalom and the subsequent insurrection of Sheba, concluding with an account of unresolved covenantal guilt from the reign of Saul.
1. The Fraught Restoration and Conflicting Motives (2 Samuel 19):
David’s grief over Absalom blinds him to the sacrifice of the men who secured his throne, prompting Joab’s harsh but politically necessary rebuke. The king’s return across the Jordan serves as a forensic sorting of hearts:
Shimei repents out of political opportunism to preserve his life once power shifts back to David.
Mephibosheth arrives unkempt in mourning, exposing Ziba’s earlier slander and demonstrating unselfish devotion by relinquishing his entire estate ("Let him take it all, since my lord the king has come safely to his house").
Barzillai the Gileadite models pure covenant loyalty, refusing royal pensions and court luxury, content simply to escort the king.
The chapter closes with toxic tribal jealousy between the ten northern tribes of Israel and the men of Judah over ceremonial ownership of the king, demonstrating that political reconciliation does not equate to spiritual unity.
2. The Anatomy of Insurrection and Pragmatic Brutality (2 Samuel 20):
The unresolved grievance of chapter 19 immediately erupts into open sedition led by Sheba, son of Bichri ("We have no share in David"). Amasa, newly appointed commander to displace Joab, demonstrates lethargy in mobilizing the militia. Joab acts with characteristic calculation and ruthlessness: he feigns a greeting of peace to murder Amasa at the great rock in Gibeon, eliminating a rival while unilaterally consolidating military command. The siege of Abel-beth-maacah highlights the contrast between Joab’s indiscriminate siege tactics and the discernment of a "wise woman" who negotiates the surrender of Sheba’s head, preserving the entire city from destruction.
3. Covenant Guilt, Atonement, and the Defeat of Giants (2 Samuel 21):
A three-year famine strikes the land. David inquires of the Lord, who reveals the cause: corporate bloodguilt incurred by Saul, who slaughtered the Gibeonites in violation of the sacred oath sworn in Joshua 9. The Gibeonites reject financial compensation and demand seven of Saul’s descendants to be executed at Gibeah. David honors the oath made to Jonathan by sparing Mephibosheth, but surrenders seven descendants. Rizpah’s vigil over the exposed corpses prompts David to retrieve the long-abandoned bones of Saul and Jonathan from Jabesh-gilead for honorable burial in the ancestral tomb of Kish, after which God heeds the prayer for the land. The chapter concludes with four battles against the remnants of the Philistine giants, where aging David is protected by his warriors, and the giants are systematically eradicated by the men of Israel.
Pillar II: Deeper Theological Meanings
1. The Inviolability of the Oath and Corporate Bloodguilt:
The famine in chapter 21 shatters the assumption that the passage of time or the death of a monarch cancels an oath made before God. Israel’s covenant with the Gibeonites had stood for over four centuries (Josh 9:15–20). Saul’s nationalistic "zeal" violated that vow, incurring objective bloodguilt (dāmîm) that attached to the land itself. God does not overlook systemic covenant-breaking to accommodate political expediency. Atonement (kāpar) required exact satisfaction: the seed of the violator had to bear the judicial consequence, establishing that divine justice is objective, legal, and trans-generational until atoned for.
2. The Counterfeit of Zeal vs. True Righteousness:
Both Saul and Joab operated under the banner of utility. Saul sought the eradication of the Gibeonites to consolidate Israelite wealth and territory; Joab murdered Abner and Amasa to maintain his unchallengeable grip on the military apparatus. Scripture draws a stark theological distinction between human ruthlessness operating under religious or political pretexts and the holy execution of divine law. Unsanctified zeal creates curses upon the land, regardless of the perpetrator's title.
3. The Sorting of Human Motives Before the King:
The crossing of the Jordan in chapter 19 prefigures the final separation of genuine allegiance from self-serving allegiance before the sovereign King:
Opportunism (Shimei): Seeks self-preservation through rapid realignment.
Mercenary loyalty (Ziba): Uses deceit to gain land and status.
True, empty-handed fidelity (Mephibosheth): Desires only the safe presence of the king, entirely indifferent to worldly spoils.
4. The Transfer of Strength and the Elimination of Strongholds:
In 2 Samuel 21:15–22, David’s physical strength fails ("David became faint"), and he is nearly slain by Ishbi-benob. The theological focus shifts: the anointed king is no longer the sole slayer of giants. His warriors—Sibbecai, Elhanan, and Jonathan son of Shimea—kill the remaining descendants of the giant in Gath. The covenant promises given to David are not sustained by the raw vitality of one man, but by the sovereign decree of God working through an obedient company who conquer the adversaries of the Kingdom.
Pillar III: The Daily Walk (Practical Application for the Seeker of Truth)
1. Honor Vows and Written Commitments Without Compromise:
The seeker of truth must recognize that God binds the conscience to all covenants, contracts, and promises, even when keeping them is inconvenient or costly. Violating an agreement under the guise of "zeal" or changing circumstances invites moral rot. A seeker’s word must remain an unbending plumb line: let your yes be yes, and your no be no.
2. Refuse Pragmatic Compromise in Defense of Truth:
Joab achieved tactical victories, but his methodology was treacherous. He assassinated his brothers-in-arms while greeting them with a kiss. The seeker must never adopt carnal, deceptive, or malicious tactics to defend spiritual truth. The defense of God's Word must be conducted with clean hands and unfeigned integrity; evil is never sanctified because it targets an adversary.
3. Examine the Heart for Self-Serving Motives:
Like Mephibosheth, the true seeker does not pursue Christ for earthly benefits, political leverage, or spiritual status. The posture of the redeemed heart asks nothing of the world’s rewards, rejoicing simply that the King reigns. Interrogate the soul continually: Am I following the Lord for the inheritance, or for the King Himself?
4. Intervene with Discernment to Quell Destruction:
The wise woman of Abel-beth-maacah demonstrates that a single person grounded in truth and discernment can arrest widespread carnage. Where contentious voices agitate for factional division and ruin, the seeker of truth uses precision, calm persuasion, and biblical fidelity to cut through emotion and dismantle rebellion at its root.
The Synthesized Message: A Guide for the Truth Seeker
The narrative of 2 Samuel 19–21 strips away romantic notions of power and reveals the uncompromising nature of divine order. Human political systems, personal ambitions, and pragmatic leaders invariably fracture:
Factional pride divides the assembly of God's people over claims of ownership (2 Sam 19:41–43).
Rebellious demagogues quickly seize on emotional discontent to declare separation (2 Sam 20:1).
Ruthless actors leverage moments of transition to eliminate rivals (2 Sam 20:9–10).
Yet above this human turmoil stands the sovereign, unchanging righteousness of the Living God. God does not forget covenants sworn in His name, nor does He permit the blood of the innocent to remain ignored. True atonement demands truth, confession, and the full satisfaction of justice.
The seeker of truth walks through a fractured world by refusing the path of Shimei’s opportunism, Ziba’s slander, Saul’s carnal zeal, and Joab’s cold violence. The seeker identifies instead with Mephibosheth’s unselfish devotion to the King, the wise woman’s courageous discernment in the face of destruction, and the loyal warriors who stand shoulder-to-shoulder to vanquish the enemies of the Lord. The final security of the faithful rests not in human strength, but in the unbreakable covenant of the King who has already made full and final atonement for His people.
The Prophetic Mirror: Modern Geopolitical Conflict
What 2 Samuel 19–21 lays bare is the lethal consequence of man attempting to execute geopolitical agendas under the banner of God while entirely discarding His holiness, His law, and His character.
When modern geopolitical conflict is viewed through the lens of Scripture, the exact patterns recorded in these chapters replay themselves on both sides:
1. The Blasphemy of Carnal Zeal (The "Saul" Syndrome):
In 2 Samuel 21, Scripture records that Saul wiped out the Gibeonites "in his zeal for the sons of Israel and Judah" (2 Sam 21:2). Notice the text does not say zeal for the glory of YHWH—it says zeal for the sons of Israel and Judah. It was ethno-nationalism wrapped in religious rhetoric. Saul justified breaking a sacred covenant sworn before the Almighty by claiming it served the survival, expansion, and security of his people.
Today, whether an ideology operates under secular realpolitik, expansionist ambitions, or religious nationalism, it is the exact same spirit: invoking divine destiny or historic entitlement while trampling underfoot the unchanging moral law of God—justice, mercy, and the protection of innocent life. God did not accept Saul’s rationale; He sent a three-year famine and demanded accountability for innocent blood spilled.
2. Bloodlust and Pagan Fatalism on the Opposing Side:
Conversely, the forces arrayed on the other side of the conflict do not operate under the God of Abraham either. Their ideology treats human life—including the lives of their own children—as cheap collateral in a campaign driven by vengeance, territorial dominion, and an uninspired religious mandate that demands blood rather than atonement.
They appeal to God’s name with their lips, but their actions mirror the pagan kings of Canaan who offered up their children to Moloch to achieve military and political power. It is hatred disguised as holy war.
3. Joab’s Pragmatism: The Deification of Power:
In 2 Samuel 20, Joab took Amasa by the beard with his right hand as if to kiss him, asked calmly, "Is it well with you, my brother?", and then gutted him with a concealed dagger. Joab was neither pro-God nor anti-God; Joab was pro-Joab. He used the monarchy, the army, and the defense of the kingdom strictly as a vehicle to consolidate his own power. He believed that the ends always justify the means, and that raw, unprincipled force is the ultimate arbiter of history.
Both sides of modern conflict rely entirely on Joab's playbook:
Strategic deception, Ruthless escalation,
Callous disregard for covenants and agreements,
Complete indifference to the carnage left in their wake, so long as the immediate objective is won.
4. The Biblical Plumb Line:
Scripture repeatedly warns what happens when people build nations, empires, or movements on injustice and blood:
Micah 3:10–11: "Who build Zion with blood and Jerusalem with iniquity... Yet they lean upon the Lord, and say, 'Is not the Lord among us? No evil can come upon us.'"
Habakkuk 2:12: "Woe to him who builds a town with blood and establishes a city by iniquity!"
Jeremiah 22:13: "Woe to him who builds his house without righteousness and his upper rooms without justice."
God is not a mascot to be drafted into human political conflicts. When men deify land, bloodline, or political dominion above the Living God, they have entered into idolatry. The tragedy unfolding is precisely what happens when opposing factions believe they are entirely justified in their own eyes, operating with unearned certainty, while neither faction bows the knee to the Prince of Peace or the objective standard of His Word.

"You Can't Always Get What You Want" is one of the most ambitious & enduring masterpieces by the Rolling Stones. Released in July 1969 as the B-side to "Honky Tonk Women" and later serving as the epic closing track to the album Let It Bleed, it is widely considered the band's poignant, philosophical farewell to the idealism of the 1960s, and anti-war. 

The Meaning: Hope Amid Disillusionment

The Core Message: While the song addresses deep disappointment, its famous chorus offers a grounded lesson in acceptance: you might not get your absolute desires, but persistent effort will secure what is truly essential to survive.

Legend: According to local folklore, it refers to Jimmy Hutmaker, a colorful town character from Excelsior, Minnesota. As the story goes, Jagger encountered him at a drugstore in 1964 where Hutmaker complained about a missing soda flavor, muttering the phrase "you can't always get what you want".  The Studio Reality: Rock historians and insiders maintain that "Mr. Jimmy" was actually a nod to Jimmy Miller, the band's genius record producer during their golden era.

The track's orchestral-rock grandeur masks immense behind-the-scenes chaos at London's Olympic Sound Studios. The Choir: Jagger wanted a gospel punch and brought in the 60-voice London Bach Choir. Arranger Jack Nitzsche double-tracked their vocals to create a towering, angelic wall of sound. Interestingly, due to the Stones' dangerous, drug-fueled reputation, the choir later requested their name be removed from the original album credits.

text:
Good morning from Virginia. 🇺🇸

On this day in 1959, a twenty-year-old former Marine walked into the American Embassy in Moscow and tried to cast off the citizenship his country had given him. Lee Harvey Oswald, born in New Orleans, raised in Fort Worth, and trained as a radar operator in the Marine Corps, arrived at the embassy on a Saturday morning, laid his passport on the receptionist’s desk, and announced that he had come to “dissolve” his American citizenship. He was not content merely to leave. He wanted the formal, legal rupture.

Consul Richard E. Snyder took him into his office. Oswald was arrogant and aggressive. He declared that his allegiance now belonged to the Soviet Union, that he had already applied for Soviet citizenship, and that he was a Marxist. He had been contemplating the step for two years. He had even offered the Soviets whatever information he possessed from his service as an aviation electronics operator. When Snyder tried to slow him down and explain the gravity of what he proposed, Oswald brushed it aside. He knew the law, he said. He did not need a lecture.

He handed over a handwritten statement, misspellings and all: “I Lee Harvey Oswald do herby request that my present citizenship in the United States of america, be revoked. I have entered the Soviet Union for the express purpose of appling for citizenship in the Soviet Union… I affirm that my ellegiance is to the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics.” The embassy retained the passport and delayed formal action. Snyder, experienced in such cases, refused to let a young man throw away his nationality on a Saturday impulse. The State Department’s standing policy was to discourage expatriation, and the consul judged correctly that renunciation, once completed, is irrevocable.

Oswald later wrote again from the Metropole Hotel, protesting the delay and repeating his demand. The Soviets never granted him the citizenship he sought, though they allowed him to remain. He worked in a radio factory in Minsk, married a Russian woman, fathered a daughter, and eventually discovered what every Western romantic who runs to a police state eventually discovers: the workers’ paradise is neither free nor particularly generous to the foreigner who arrives expecting to be treated as a hero. By 1962 he was writing the embassy asking to come home, claiming disillusionment, and asserting that he had never really sought Soviet citizenship after all. The country he had tried to renounce took him back.

The episode is a small, sharp window onto the Cold War. Here was a young American, trained and equipped by his own government, volunteering both his loyalty and his technical knowledge to the principal adversary of the United States. The embassy’s refusal to complete the renunciation that day was not bureaucratic pettiness; it was the prudent exercise of national interest. Citizenship is not a costume to be discarded when ideology strikes. It is a bond, and the man who treats it as disposable has already revealed the shallowness of his character.

Oswald’s later return and the events that followed in Dallas only deepen the irony. The system he once praised and the country he once sought to abandon collided in ways no one in that Moscow office on October 31, 1959, could have fully foreseen. What remains clear is the simple fact of that Saturday morning: an American Marine stood before his own consul and offered to trade the citizenship of a free republic for the citizenship of a dictatorship. The consul said not today.

America 250 🇺🇸

text:
God made the night hours for sleep, not prayer.

There is absolutely nothing wrong with praying at night. 

If you choose to pray at midnight, 2 a.m., or 4 a.m., there is nothing wrong with that.

However, there is no scriptural basis for teaching that prayers offered at night have greater spiritual benefits, carry more power, or produce better results than prayers offered during the day.

Prayer is not more effective because of the hour of the day.

Yes, we find people in the Scriptures praying at night. 

We also find people praying during the day, in the morning, and at different hours. 

But none of these establishes a spiritual hierarchy of prayer hours.

In fact, Scripture teaches us to pray at all times.

Ephesians 6:18 — Praying always with all prayer and supplication.

1 Thessalonians 5:17 — Pray without ceasing.

Luke 18:1 — Men ought always to pray and not to faint.

Acts 3:1 — Peter and John went up together into the temple at the hour of prayer, being the ninth hour.

The emphasis is on a consistent life of prayer, not on discovering a supposedly more powerful hour.

God is not more available at midnight than He is at midday. 

The Holy Spirit does not become more active because it is 1 a.m. 

Spiritual realities are not governed by the clock.

Please, don't allow anyone to manufacture a vain, imaginary, and pseudo-spiritual culture around night vigils, midnight prayers, and particular prayer hours.

If you want to pray at night, pray. 

But don't do it because someone has convinced you that God is more accessible at that hour.

And please, take your sleep seriously.

Sleep is not a sign of spiritual weakness. 

Rest is not a demonstration of carnality. 

God created the human body with the need for rest, and Scripture itself recognises the value of sleep.

Psalm 127:2 says that God gives His beloved sleep.

Even Jesus slept in a boat (Mark 4:38).

You don't have to deprive yourself of sleep to prove that you are spiritually serious.

Christian spirituality is not measured by how many hours of sleep you sacrifice or how many nights you can stay awake.

Build a consistent life of prayer. Study the Scriptures. Grow in the knowledge of Christ. 

Walk in love. And when it is time to sleep, sleep.

You are not less spiritual because you slept through the night.

Please, sleep on time and sleep well.

May God give you understanding.

Apostle Oluwashina Akinnagbe

text:
A QUESTION ON SPIRITS
Question: "If I see or feel the presence of negative spirits around me, how do I send them away? And what if they refuse to leave?"

Answer: Why send them away? Just leave them alone. Let them stay and listen to your Nembutsu, let them hear your thoughts and words of faith. One day, they will become bored with a guy like you who minds his own business and constantly says Nembutsu, or even better, they might be influenced by your devotion and entrust to Amida themselves. In Jodo Shinshu we do not exorcize, nor fight with spirits, rather we convert them by our example. The urge of Shinran, "receive yourself faith and help others receive faith" applies to them, too.

It is good to be friendly towards the spirit world. Realize that spirits, ghosts and various types of nonhuman beings inhabit the same space with us. Your land is their land, too. Some are in the same place for hundreds or thousands of years, so they have the same right as you to be here. Who are you to tell them to go away? Let them be and focus on living a life of gratitude with as little damage as possible to other beings, and focus on Nembutsu.

All beings suffer, no matter they are humans or non-humans. Some spirits may like you, feel neutral towards you or may be inclined to hate you due to karma from the past. No problem! Let them hate you, while you just focus on Nembutsu. How much can somebody hate another person if that one does not respond to the hate and minds his own business?

Offer incense to Amida Buddha in the name of all beings, including the spirits of the place you live, and make aspirations for them - may they be healthy in body and mind, always receive whatever is necessary and beneficial for them. May all their obstacles be removed and may they create indestructible connections with Amida Buddha, entrust to Him, say His Name (Namo Amida Bu) and wish to be born in His Pure Land[1]. Also pray to Amida to help them, although He already tries His best to help. However, if you pray for them, they will feel your good intentions.

If you think this way, if you say Nembutsu and have devotion and faith, the invisible beings who happen to live there or just pass through will know your thoughts and might be inspired to entrust to Amida and say Nembutsu themselves, and if not, they will finally leave you alone as they see that you are no threat to them. In fact, they cannot harm you even if they try, because if you have faith (shinjin) you automatically benefit from the protection of Amida and all Buddhas.

So again, no matter what you see, hear, or feel around you, just focus on Nembutsu and mind your own business.

Before the Dhvajarohanam, an elaborate Puja was performed to the Dhvajastambha and Dhvaja by the Jagadguru, and the Chief Minister also performed Pushparchana to the Dhvajastambha and Dhvaja.

Preceding this sacred ceremony, Jagadguru Shankaracharya Mahaswamiji performed elaborate Puja to Bhagavan Sri Trimbakeshwar with the chanting of the sacred Rudra and connected Veda Mantras.

After the inauguration of the Simhastha Kumbh Mela at the Shubha Muhurta at Kushavarta Tirtha, the Hon’ble Chief Minister of Maharashtra, Sri Devendra Fadnavis, and his wife, Smt. Amruta Fadnavis, offered their reverential salutations to the Jagadguru and were blessed by the Jagadguru with a beautiful idol of Sri Sharadamba and a replica of the Vidyashankara Temple.

MiniMax-H3 prompt👇
integrated_multimodal_description

15-second widescreen I2VA live-action coastal training scene. Use <Picture 1> as the only reference: same adult woman A, face, cap, loose cropped T-shirt, tied swimwear, athletic proportions, skin tone, sweat sheen, coastal stone path, palms, stone wall, ocean, and original warm coastal light. One continuous path only. Ocean stays left-rear; stone wall and palms stay right; path center is the fixed jump point. B is an offscreen friend only through nearby English voice, laughter, footsteps, and slight handheld camera movement; B never appears clearly. No new visible people, new location, subtitles, text, logos, watermark, fade, or black ending.

A's emotional path: confident half-smile -> teased by B -> focused preparation -> controlled jump -> proud breath-laugh after landing -> intimate encouragement. She is playful, athletic, grounded, never theatrical. Eyes move before head and mouth. Hair, cap-edge strands, T-shirt hem, swimwear ties, jewelry, sweat sheen, and body follow wind, gravity, breath, jump force, and settling.

Stable sea wind blows from left-rear ocean toward the path, affecting hair, loose hem, waist ties, and palms. Jump takeoff shakes tiny droplets and grains from damp stone seams; landing spreads a small water mark and low grit movement. Backlit sea haze stays thin and transparent. No smoke wall, explosions, energy, or decorative particles.

Light: 4300K-4800K warm side-backlight from upper-left/rear, cool cyan ocean fill from front, shaped wall shadow on right, slow palm shadows across shoulders, clothing, abdomen, and wall. Palette: sand gold #C9A063, bronze skin #A66B45, deep ocean teal #254F57, palm-shadow olive #3E4A32, wet-stone charcoal #2B2D2B. Controlled saturation, warm natural skin, teal shadows with lifted blacks, soft highlight roll-off, fine cinematic grain, no plastic smoothing.

[00:00-00:02.00] Ground-level lateral tracking along damp stone near the wall. Start on A's steps, pass her tied waist swimwear and wind-lifted cropped T-shirt hem, arrive at medium view. A walks forward, right hand makes one practical waist-tie adjustment, left shoulder brushes the wall. Eyes look down first; one mouth corner forms a tiny confident curve. B offscreen: <d>[English] Showing off already? </d>

[00:02.00-00:04.00] Camera pushes from waist height to medium-close upper body and face. At the path center, A stops; shoulders release, breath expands chest, core firms, knees bend slightly. Eyes rise to B first, one brow tail lifts, then head follows. Smile becomes mildly challenging. A replies: <d>[English] Not showing off. Just proving it works. </d> Wind lifts the T-shirt hem on inhale, then it settles as she braces.

[00:04.00-00:05.40] Low-angle upward shot. A drops into a controlled squat, swings both arms back then upward, and drives into one vertical standing jump from the fixed path center. Camera pushes during loading and pulls out slightly at takeoff. Brows focus, lips close naturally, no theatrical strain. At foot release, small droplets and grains scatter outward, arc briefly, and flash in side-backlight.

At apex, A looks down toward B with lowered upper eyelids and a small confident mouth curve. Now you're in. </d> Hold A facing B while cap strands, T-shirt hem, and waist ties move in sea wind; surf, palms, and footfalls continue. No fade or black.

1/19 | INVESTIGATION — THE UAE’S SECRET CHANNEL TO WASHINGTON

A newly published book, Princes and Thieves, by investigative journalist Matthew Cole examines how Mohammed bin Zayed (MBZ) cultivated Jared Kushner to influence US policy in the Middle East.

2/19 | THE SECRET MEETING

On 15 December 2016, weeks before Donald Trump’s inauguration, MBZ met Kushner and senior Trump advisers at New York’s Four Seasons Hotel.

The meeting took place away from the public spotlight, bypassing conventional diplomatic channels.

3/19 | AN UNUSUAL DELEGATION

Cole’s account describes MBZ arriving with a large Emirati delegation, reportedly including armed security personnel.

He had also allegedly cancelled a planned farewell engagement with outgoing President Barack Obama.

Instead, his attention turned to Trump’s inner circle.

4/19 | BYPASSING THE OBAMA WHITE HOUSE

The UAE did not provide the customary advance notification of MBZ’s visit.

The Obama administration reportedly discovered the trip through diplomatic flight information.

The episode raised questions about protocol and Abu Dhabi’s direct outreach to the incoming administration.

5/19 | THE FINANCIAL CONNECTION

According to Cole, a New York hedge-fund manager with financial ties to the UAE and a personal friendship with Kushner helped arrange the meeting.

The episode illustrates how private financial relationships could provide access to powerful US political figures.

6/19 | KUSHNER’S MIDDLE EAST ROLE

Cole reports that Kushner told MBZ the Middle East would be a major foreign-policy priority for the incoming Trump administration.

Kushner also indicated he would personally oversee efforts related to the Israeli–Palestinian conflict, despite limited diplomatic experience.

7/19 | THE ARAB SPRING

MBZ reportedly criticised Obama’s response to the Arab Spring, particularly the 2011 uprising that removed Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak.

He viewed Washington’s abandonment of Mubarak as a betrayal of a strategic ally and a warning about the reliability of US security guarantees.

8/19 | IRAQ AND THE RISE OF ISIS

MBZ also argued that the American withdrawal from Iraq had created a strategic vacuum, allowing ISIS to expand across Iraq and Syria.

He presented this interpretation as evidence of weaknesses in Obama’s Middle East policy.

9/19 | THE UAE’S TWO PRINCIPAL ADVERSARIES

According to the book, MBZ identified two major threats to the UAE:

• The Muslim Brotherhood, representing political Islam.

• Iran, through its regional influence and relationships with armed groups.

These concerns shaped his approach to Washington.

10/19 | THE QATAR QUESTION

MBZ reportedly accused Qatar of financing the Muslim Brotherhood and using Al Jazeera to intensify regional tensions and support Islamist movements.

He wanted the incoming Trump administration to confront Doha.

These allegations reflected the UAE leadership’s position, not independently established findings.

11/19 | THE IRAN NUCLEAR AGREEMENT

MBZ strongly criticised the 2015 nuclear deal between Iran and world powers.

He reportedly argued that Tehran could evade nuclear restrictions and use sanctions relief to strengthen its regional position.

He sought a tougher American policy towards Iran.

12/19 | THE MAP OF IRANIAN INFLUENCE

Cole describes MBZ presenting Kushner with a map highlighting Hezbollah in Lebanon, the Houthis in Yemen and Hamas in Gaza.

MBZ portrayed these movements as part of Iran’s regional influence network, reflecting his assessment of the geopolitical threat.

13/19 | TESTING THE TRUMP ADMINISTRATION

The book argues that MBZ’s criticisms of Obama closely matched positions expressed during Trump’s presidential campaign.

The meeting therefore offered Abu Dhabi an opportunity to test ideological alignment and identify influential figures within the incoming administration.1/2

🌍 OCTOBER 31 - FOLLOW THE CAPITAL
🚨 UPT0BER NEVER ARRIVED
🇪🇺A EUROPEAN CONSTITUTIONAL CRISIS DID

🗣️ And somehow, people are still arguing about Bitcoin's four-year cycle

📊 Look at how October actually ended
- 🇵🇱 Poland's president turned his plane around as police surrounded the Constitutional Tribunal
- 🇫🇷 France received another warning about its government debt
- 🇨🇳 China's manufacturing activity contracted again
- 🛢️ Oil companies are earning extraordinary profits while fuel shortages persist
- 🤖 Intel suffered its worst stock-market collapse in decades
- 🥇 Gold fell below $3,900
- ✴️ Bitcoin is heading toward a negative October

🏛️ AND THE FED ALREADY HELD RATES UNCHANGED

THESE ARE NOT TEN DIFFERENT CRISES
🌍 They're different parts of a world fighting over:
- 🔋POWER
- 🛡️SECURITY
- 🏗️PRODUCTION
- 💵AND CAPITAL

📊 Here's what the end of October actually revealed

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
1) 🇵🇱 POLAND: THIS IS BIGGER THAN ANOTHER EUROPEAN PROTEST

✈️ On Friday, Polish President Karol Nawrocki interrupted his flight to Senegal

Why?
- 🏛️ A confrontation erupted around Poland's Constitutional Tribunal
- 🛑 Its disputed president was suspended
- 👮 Police deployed around the court
- 💥 Protesters clashed with officers

🗣️ And opposition politicians accused Donald Tusk's government of staging a coup

⚠️ IMPORTANT:
📋 A constitutional crisis is confirmed
🙅 A completed coup is NOT an independently established fact
⚖️ Poland's rival political camps dispute who has lawful authority over the court

💡 And that's precisely why the story matters
💡 THE QUESTION ISN'T ONLY WHO CONTROLS THE BUILDING
🔍 It's: WHO HAS THE AUTHORITY TO DECIDE WHAT IS LEGAL?

⏳ When political institutions disagree over that question, uncertainty can extend into:
- 📋 Legislation
- 🏛️ Government decisions
- 💼 Business regulation
- 📜 Contract enforcement
- 💵 Investment confidence

🙅 That doesn't prove capital is fleeing Poland
🧱 But it creates a risk investors cannot ignore

💰 CAPITAL IMPLICATION:
📈 Political uncertainty ↑
📉 Institutional predictability ↓
📊 Potential risk premium ↑ if the crisis persists

🎯 A COUNTRY DOESN'T NEED TO DEFAULT TO BECOME A RISKIER PLACE TO INVEST

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
2) 🇫🇷 FRANCE: EVEN GOVERNMENTS ARE LOSING THE BENEFIT OF THE DOUBT

💡 Now connect Poland's political confrontation to France's financial problems

📢 Fitch just changed France's credit outlook to: 
⚠️ NEGATIVE
📉 Its A+ rating remains unchanged
🚨But the warning is serious

📊 France's economy unexpectedly contracted in Q3:
 -0.1%

🏛️ Government debt is projected to rise toward: 
124% of GDP by 2028

💳 And borrowing costs remain elevated

💡 HERE'S THE TRAP

🔍 Governments need money to address:
- ⚡ Energy costs
- 🛡️ Defense
- 🏠 Social pressure
- 🇺🇦 Ukraine
- 📜 Existing debt

🧱 But the more expensive borrowing becomes, the less room remains for everything else

🔄 THE CHAIN:
📉 Weak growth
↓
💵 Tax revenue pressure
↓
💸 Fiscal deficits remain difficult
↓
📜 Investors demand compensation for risk
↓
📈 Government interest costs ↑
↓
🛑 Less flexibility to support growth

⚖️ Now add political fragmentation
Reforming the budget becomes even harder

💰 CAPITAL IMPLICATION:
📜 Sovereign borrowing costs ↑
🏛️ Fiscal flexibility ↓
💶 Investors become more selective between European governments

🎯 EUROPE'S PROBLEM ISN'T JUST FINDING MONEY
🧱 IT'S KEEPING THE COST OF THAT MONEY UNDER CONTROL

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
3) 🇪🇺🇨🇦 BUT EUROPE JUST MADE A MAJOR STRATEGIC MOVE

🤝 Canada and the EU launched an: 
🌍 ALLIANCE FOR THE FUTURE

🔍 The priorities?
- ⚡ Energy
- 🪨 Critical minerals
- 🤖 Artificial intelligence
- 🛡️ Security
- 💳 Financial systems
- 📡 Digital infrastructure
- 🇨🇦 Canada is also pursuing a new form of closer association with the EU

⚠️ NOT FULL EU MEMBERSHIP
⚖️ And the legal meaning of any future associate status is still being negotiated

💡 NOW CONNECT THIS TO THE BIGGER WORLD
🇺🇸🇯🇵🇰🇷 The US, Japan and South Korea also signed an Arctic-Pacific partnership

❓ Why are governments suddenly so interested in:
- ❄️ The Arctic
- 🚢 Trade routes
- 🪨 Minerals
- 📡 Communications
- ⚡ Energy independence

🧱 Because countries increasingly want alternatives to depending on any single strategic partner

💡 THIS IS THE SHIFT
🌍 The old model: Buy from whoever offers the lowest price
🛡️ The emerging model: Build relationships that still work during a crisis

💰 CAPITAL IMPLICATION:
🏗️ Alternative infrastructure ↑
🪨 Strategic mineral investment ↑
📡 Independent communications ↑
🚢 New transport routes ↑

🎯 THE WORLD ISN'T FORMALLY DIVIDED INTO THREE EMPIRES
🧱 BUT COUNTRIES ARE ALREADY BUILDING SYSTEMS THAT REDUCE THEIR DEPENDENCE ON ONE ANOTHER

📈 That's where future capital commitments can become enormous

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
4) 🇨🇳 CHINA JUST EXPOSED ITS OTHER ECONOMY

🇨🇳 China's official October manufacturing PMI: 
📉 49.3
📊 Below 50 means activity is contracting compared with the previous month

🔍 But the more interesting numbers are underneath:
📉 Small businesses: 47.5
📉 New manufacturing orders: 49.4
📉 Composite activity: 49.7

💡 NOW THINK ABOUT THE CONTRADICTION

⚖️ China is becoming more competitive in selected global industries:
- 🚗 Electric vehicles
- 🤖 AI
- 💾 Technology
- 🏭 Advanced manufacturing

⚠️ But its broader domestic economy remains under pressure

❓ HOW CAN BOTH BE TRUE?
🙅 Because industrial success doesn't automatically create strong household demand

🔄 THE CHAIN:
📉 Weak domestic spending
↓
🚢 Businesses depend more on exports
↓
📈 Chinese products compete harder abroad
↓
🛡️ Foreign governments protect domestic industries
↓
🧱 Trade tensions rise
↓
🇨🇳 China invests more in strategic self-sufficiency

💵 That's expensive for everyone

🇪🇺 And it helps explain why Europe is seeking new mineral suppliers and industrial partnerships

💰 CAPITAL IMPLICATION:
🇨🇳 Strategic sectors retain priority
🏠 Domestic-demand businesses remain vulnerable
🌍 Other countries spend more to reduce dependence on Chinese supply chains

🎯 CHINA CANBECOME MORE POWERFUL INDUSTRIALLY WHILE ITS DOMESTIC ECONOMY WEAKENS
🧱 Both can happen at once

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
5) 🛢️ THE ENERGY MARKET HAS A PROBLEM OIL PRICES ALONE DON'T EXPLAIN

💡 This is one of October's most important economic lessons

🛢️ Oil can move through shipping routes again... while diesel remains extremely expensive

🐚 Exxon and Chevron just reported exceptional profits from refining

❓ Why? 
🛢️Because crude oil and usable fuel are not the same thing

🧱 YOU CAN HAVE BARRELS OF OIL WITHOUT ENOUGH WORKING REFINERIES

🔍 And the distinction matters:
⚓ Crude supply
↓
🏭 Refining capacity
↓
⛽ Diesel and gasoline
↓
🚚 Transport and industry

💥 A disruption at any stage changes the final price

- ❄️ Meanwhile Europe enters winter with gas storage around: 📦 75%
- 🇩🇪 Germany's storage is considerably lower
- 📜 And the EU is still committed to phasing out Russian gas

💡 SO EVEN IF IRAN REOPENS SHIPPING...
🙅 Damaged refineries don't instantly restart
💸 Insurance doesn't immediately become cheap
🏗️ Replacement infrastructure doesn't pay for itself overnight

💰 CAPITAL IMPLICATION:
⛽ Refining capacity ↑ in strategic value
📦 Energy inventories ↑
⚡ Alternative energy supply ↑
🏭 Energy-dependent industries remain exposed

🎯 THE IMPORTANT QUESTION ISN'T ONLY WHETHER OIL FALLS
🧱 IT'S WHETHER THE COST OF PRODUCING AND DELIVERING ENERGY ACTUALLY FALLS

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
6) 🇮🇷🇺🇦 DIPLOMACY IS ACTIVE
⚔️SO IS PREPARATION FOR MORE CONFLICT

🤝 The US, Iran are still negotiating through intermediaries
🇶🇦 Qatari mediators have been holding intensive discussions

⚠️ But the central disagreement remains:
🇺🇸 Washington wants nuclear concessions
🇮🇷 Tehran wants sanctions relief and other conditions addressed first
🪖 At the same time, Washington and Israel have prepared military options

⚠️ A REPORTED ATTACK PLAN IS NOT A CONFIRMED ATTACK ORDER
💵 But preparing for war costs money even when no attack takes place

🇺🇦 Now look at Ukraine
🇷🇺🇺🇸 The US, Russia and Ukraine continue preparing potential negotiations

⚠️ Yet:
❌ No final date
❌ No comprehensive ceasefire
❌ No territorial settlement
❌ No lasting security guarantees

🤝 The humanitarian arrangement around Oleshky is meaningful
🙅 But a local humanitarian pause is not a national peace agreement
🇪🇺 And Europe still wants a role in decisions that could shape its security for decades

💡 HERE'S THE CONNECTION:
💬 Diplomacy creates a possibility of future relief
🏗️ Military preparation creates expenses today

💰 CAPITAL IMPLICATION:
- 🛡️ Defense and readiness spending continue
- 🛢️ Energy risk premiums remain relevant
- 🇪🇺 Long-term security financing remains necessary

🎯 NEGOTIATIONS CAN IMPROVE EXPECTATIONS
🧱 ONLY A DURABLE SETTLEMENT CAN START CHANGING THE ACTUAL OBLIGATIONS

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
7) 🏦 THIS IS WHY THE FED DIDN'T SAVE OCTOBER

🏦 The Fed held rates unchanged

⚠️ And yet:
📉 Technology stocks sold off
🥇 Gold fell
✴️ Crypto weakened

❓ Why? Because stopping rate hikes doesn't automatically produce a new wave of cheap capital

💪 The US economy is still growing
🔥 Inflation remains elevated
🏛️ Government borrowing remains enormous
💳 And corporate financing requirements are expanding

💡 WATCH WHAT HAPPENED TO GOLD
📉 Gold fell below: $3,900 despite geopolitical uncertainty
❓ Does that mean gold has stopped being a defensive asset?
🙅 No

🔍 It means defensive assets can be sold when:
💵 Investors need cash
📉 Portfolios suffer losses
💳 Leverage has to be reduced
📜 Yield-bearing alternatives are competitive

🔄 THE CHAIN:
📈 Financial pressure ↑
↓
💧 Demand for liquidity ↑
↓
🛒 Investors sell what they can sell
↓
⚖️ Even traditionally defensive assets can fall

💰 CAPITAL IMPLICATION:
💵 Liquidity becomes valuable
📜 High-quality bonds remain competitive
⚠️ Leveraged investors face additional risk

🎯 DURING A LIQUIDITY SQUEEZE, EVEN A GOOD ASSET CAN BECOME A SOURCE OF CASH

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
8) 🤖 AI JUST LEARNED THAT BILLIONS IN REVENUE AREN'T ENOUGH

💻 Intel fell almost:
 📉 29% in one session
📊 Its worst one-day decline in decades

🔍 The problem?
- 📉 Weak guidance
- 📈 High costs
- 💵 Cash consumption

❓ And investor doubts about the economics of its expansion

🤖 Meanwhile Big Tech is still spending extraordinary amounts on AI
🌐 Amazon, Meta, Microsoft and Alphabet continue financing enormous infrastructure projects

⚠️ BUT THE MARKET IS STARTING TO ASK A DIFFERENT QUESTION
🙅 Not: IS AI THE FUTURE?
🔍 But: WHO WILL ACTUALLY KEEP THE PROFITS?

🧠 Think about it:
🤖 AI demand grows
↓
⚡ Power demand grows
↓
💾 Chip demand grows
↓
🏗️ Data-centre spending grows
↓
💳 Financing needs grow

⏳ And only after that:
💰 Customers have to generate enough value to justify the expense
💡 THE BILL ARRIVES BEFORE ALL THE PROFITS DO

💵 Some suppliers collect cash immediately
🔮 Some AI developers and infrastructure operators need years to earn back their investments

💰 CAPITAL IMPLICATION:
⬆️ Proven cash-generating suppliers ↑
🏢 Scarce infrastructure ↑
💳 Businesses dependent on continuous financing ↓

🎯 AI DOESN'T HAVE TO FAIL FOR ITS INVESTORS TO LOSE MONEY
🧱 The price paid for future success still matters

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
9) ✴️ UPT0BER IS THE PERFECT EXAMPLE OF WHY WE FOLLOW CAPITAL, NOT CALENDARS

🟠 Bitcoin is heading toward a negative October
📉 That was already becoming clear before the Binance hack
💥 Then came a genuine: $6.3B security incident
🕵️‍♂️ Investigators have linked the attack to North Korean hackers with high confidence

⚠️ But attribution is not the same thing as a completed investigation
🛡️ Binance says it will cover customer losses
🧊 And roughly half the affected assets were frozen

⚠️ THE HACK WAS REAL
🙅 But it doesn't explain every weakness that came before it

📊 Look at the broader environment:
🏦 Financing remained expensive
🤖 Technology valuations came under pressure
💵 Investors became more selective
📉 Crypto trading participation weakened
⏳ And the October rally never developed the consistent demand required to change the picture

💡 NOW ADD THE BIGGEST PARADOX:
- 🏦 Banks are adopting blockchain
- 💵 Stablecoins are expanding
- 📊 Traditional securities are being tokenized
- 🔗 Financial infrastructure is becoming more digital

🙅 BUT THE SYSTEM DOESN'T AUTOMATICALLY NEED TO BUY YOUR TOKEN

💡 A useful technology can attract capital without distributing that value equally to every asset associated with it

💰 CAPITAL IMPLICATION:
- 🔗 Financial infrastructure ↑
- 🔐 Security and custody ↑
- 🏦 Institutional adoption ↑

⚠️ BUT:
🟠 Broad speculative demand -> still unproven
🎰 Fragile liquidity -> still vulnerable

🎯 THE BINANCE HACK MADE A WEAK MARKET WEAKER
🧱 IT DIDN'T CREATE OCTOBER'S ENTIRE MACRO ENVIRONMENT

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
🏁 SO WHAT DID OCTOBER ACTUALLY TEACH US?

- 🇵🇱 Political institutions can become another source of uncertainty
- 🇫🇷 Governments can struggle to finance their obligations
- 🇨🇳 Industrial strength can hide weak domestic demand
- 🇪🇺 Alliances can reorganize even without formal geopolitical agreements
- 🛢️ Expensive energy can reward suppliers while damaging customers
- 🇮🇷 Peace talks can continue alongside military preparations
- 🤖 Technological growth can require more capital than expected
- ✴️ Blockchain adoption can accelerate while speculative asset prices fall

💡 NOW CONNECT EVERYTHING
🌐THE WORLD IS PAYING MORE TO BECOME LESS DEPENDENT

Less dependent on:
- ⚡ One energy supplier
- 🌍 One geopolitical partner
- 📡 One communications network
- 💾 One technology ecosystem

text:
🎃👻🍂 HAPPY HALLOWEEN, HALLOWE'EN, ALL HALLOWS' EVE OR SAMHAIN 🍂👻🎃FROM ANCIENT GAELIC TRADITIONS TO TURNIP LANTERNS, SUPERNATURAL CREATURES AND ROBERT BURNS THE FASCINATING HISTORY BEHIND HALLOWEEN!

Tonight, millions of people will carve pumpkins, dress in costumes, tell ghost stories and enjoy a little Halloween mischief.... have you ever wondered where these traditions actually came from?

Long before pumpkins became popular, and centuries before modern trick-or-treating, communities across Britain and Ireland marked this time of year with seasonal gatherings, mysterious folklore, religious observances and some wonderfully peculiar customs.
And the history is even more fascinating than the legends! 🧡

SAMHAIN WHEN SUMMER GAVE WAY TO WINTER
One of Halloween's most important historical connections is the ancient Gaelic festival of Samhain.
Traditionally associated with 1st November, with celebrations beginning the evening before, Samhain marked the transition from summer into winter.

Pronounced approximately "SOW-in", it was a significant turning point in the traditional Irish calendar. The harvest was ending. Livestock were being brought in from summer grazing. Food and fuel needed to be stored. Families were preparing for shorter days, colder nights and the difficulties of winter.

In early Irish literature, Samhain and Beltane, celebrated around the beginning of May, marked the division between the winter and summer portions of the year. For farming communities, these seasonal changes mattered enormously. And Samhain was associated with something else...

THE SUPERNATURAL! 👻
In Irish mythology and later folklore, Samhain became associated with unusual encounters between the ordinary world and the mysterious Otherworld.

The Otherworld was believed to be inhabited by supernatural beings, including the aos sí, sometimes associated with ancient burial mounds, hills and fairy forts. Stories told of spirits visiting familiar places, mysterious beings travelling after dark and strange happenings on lonely roads.

Some traditions suggested that departed relatives might return to their former homes. Others warned that less welcome visitors could also be wandering about! People sometimes left food for returning spirits or observed protective customs around their homes.
Although these beliefs are well documented in Irish folklore, much of our written evidence comes from centuries later.

BONFIRES, DRUIDS AND ANCIENT MYSTERIES
Fire has long been associated with autumn and winter celebrations. Later traditions connected Samhain with bonfires, community gatherings and protection against supernatural dangers. You may have heard stories of Druids gathering around enormous sacred fires and every household relighting its hearth from their embers.

It's a wonderful image! What we can say with confidence is that Samhain marked a major seasonal boundary in Gaelic tradition. And that alone makes it an extraordinary part of our history.

BEWARE THE PÚCA!
One of the most entertaining creatures of Irish folklore is the púca. A mysterious, shape-shifting being that might appear as a horse, goat, dog or another animal.

Depending on the story, the púca could be mischievous, frightening or surprisingly helpful. Imagine walking along a lonely country lane on a dark autumn evening, hearing strange noises and remembering all those stories about supernatural creatures! It's hardly surprising that these legends survived for generations. 

ALL HALLOWS' EVE  THE CHRISTIAN CONNECTION
As Christianity spread and developed across Britain and Ireland, the end of October also became associated with important Christian observances.
1 NOVEMBER ALL SAINTS' DAY, also known as All Hallows' Day or Hallowmas.
2 NOVEMBER ALL SOULS' DAY, traditionally associated with prayers and remembrance for the departed.

The evening before All Saints' Day became known as All Hallows' Eve. Over time, the name was shortened to Hallowe'en and eventually Halloween. This is where our modern word comes from!

The relationship between Samhain and the Christian calendar is complicated. It is sometimes claimed that the Church simply took over a pagan festival and renamed it... it was likely not such a straightforward explanation.

The celebrations we recognise today developed through centuries of religious practice, regional folklore and changing social customs.

SOULING AN ENGLISH HALLOWEEN TRADITION
Here's a fascinating custom from medieval England. Around All Souls' Day, poorer members of the community sometimes went from house to house asking for food or charity. In return, they offered prayers for deceased relatives of those who gave to them.

Small cakes, often known as soul cakes, became associated with the custom. This tradition of souling survived in some areas long after the Middle Ages.
It is one of several door-to-door customs that historians discuss when tracing the development of modern Halloween activities.

BEFORE PUMPKINS, WE CARVED TURNIPS!
Long before the familiar orange pumpkin became the symbol of Halloween, people in the UK and Ireland carved frightening faces into turnips and other root vegetables. In Scotland, these were often called neep lanterns.

The turnip was hollowed out, a face carved into its skin and a candle placed inside. The result could be genuinely terrifying! And anyone who has ever tried hollowing out a turnip will know just how difficult it can be (my dad had the scooping out job when we were young.. turnips are tough! 😂

As Halloween customs travelled to North America, pumpkins became an increasingly popular alternative.
They were larger, softer and considerably easier to carve. And so the familiar glowing pumpkin gradually became one of the world's most recognisable Halloween symbols.

GUISING SCOTLAND'S TRADITION BEFORE MODERN TRICK-OR-TREATING
In Scotland, children traditionally went guising. They dressed in costumes or disguises and visited neighbours, often performing a song, joke, poem or little party trick in return for a treat. And here's the important difference from some modern trick-or-treating... 

YOU HAD TO EARN YOUR SWEETS! Treats might include fruit, nuts, cakes or small gifts. The tradition survived for generations, and many Scottish families still remember having to perform something before receiving their reward. So while modern trick-or-treating has strong North American influences, Britain and Ireland already had their own door-to-door Halloween customs.

APPLES, NUTS AND FINDING YOUR FUTURE HUSBAND!
Halloween wasn't always about frightening people.
It was also associated with games, romance and fortune-telling. Bobbing for apples was a popular amusement.
Nuts were placed near a fire, with their behaviour supposedly revealing whether a romantic relationship would succeed.
And in parts of Scotland, young people participated in a particularly peculiar tradition...
PULLING KALE STALKS FROM THE GROUND!

According to folklore, the size, shape and condition of the stalk could reveal details about a future husband or wife. Even the amount of soil clinging to the roots supposedly indicated whether that future partner would be wealthy! Imagine someone today announcing they'd been out pulling vegetables to discover whom they were going to marry! 

ROBERT BURNS AND THE HALLOWEEN TRADITIONS OF SCOTLAND
One of the most wonderful historical records of these customs comes from Scotland's national poet, Robert Burns. In 1785, Burns wrote his poem Halloween, first published the following year. The poem describes the games, beliefs, romantic superstitions and celebrations of rural Ayrshire. Burns even included explanatory notes to help readers understand the traditions. Among the customs he described were burning nuts, pulling kale stalks and attempting to predict future relationships. He captured a world in which Halloween was an evening of laughter, community gatherings and mysterious possibilities.
Some merry, friendly, country folk gathering to enjoy themselves, just as generations had done before them. His poem remains a wonderful historical record of Scottish folklore.

FROM ANCIENT SEASONAL TRADITIONS TO MODERN HALLOWEEN

Halloween as we know it today was not created by one community, one religion or one historical event.
It developed over many centuries. Ancient Gaelic seasonal traditions contributed the association with winter and the supernatural. Christian observances contributed the name All Hallows' Eve and traditions of remembrance. Irish, Scottish and English communities preserved customs involving lanterns, disguises, food, games and visiting neighbours.
And later, particularly through North American popular culture, pumpkins, costumes and trick-or-treating helped shape the celebrations familiar today.

Some traditions have disappeared.
Others survive in families and communities.
And many have changed beyond recognition.
But beneath the modern decorations and sweets lies a remarkable collection of cultural history.

🎃👻 SO, HAPPY HALLOWEEN, HALLOWE'EN, ALL HALLOWS' EVE AND SAMHAIN TO THOSE WHO OBSERVE IT!

Whether you're carving a pumpkin, or turnip; remembering someone you've lost, celebrating an ancient seasonal tradition, taking the children trick-or-treating or simply enjoying a cosy autumn evening, have a wonderful time.

Did you carve pumpkins or turnips growing up?
Did you go guising in Scotland and have to sing or tell a joke for your treats?
Did you play apple-bobbing games or burn nuts to predict your romantic future?
Were you told stories about the púca, fairies or other mysterious creatures?

Or are you firmly in the "lights off, curtains closed, pretend nobody's home" camp?

text:
A hacker group just apologized for a ransomware attack on a New Mexico hospital and offered patients up to $2,500 each. Here's what you need to know.

The University of New Mexico Health Sciences Center disclosed a cyberattack that caused system outages and disrupted patient care and surgeries. It is New Mexico's only Level I trauma center. The incident was detected on October 26, 2026. As a precaution, all ambulance traffic was temporarily diverted to other hospitals.

Then the group that claimed the attack said sorry. Reports name the ransomware group as BYOD. They say they have "morals" and "are not villains". They say they did not realize some of the computers they hit were machines supporting patients in real time.

The offer has two parts. They are giving out free decryption keys. They will also pay up to $2,500 to any affected patient who sends proof. They say the money is for the inconvenience. But they say they will keep the stolen data.

UNM Health has warned patients that the compensation offer could be a scam. The worry is that patients could be tricked into handing over personal data, financial details or ID documents. That could lead to identity theft or other fraud.

Online reaction is split. Some people joke that even hackers show more morals than officials. Others say $2,500 is small, and that nobody should attack a hospital at all.

Key numbers:
- Up to $2,500 offered per affected patient
- Attack detected October 26, 2026
- New Mexico's only Level I trauma center hit
- Ambulance traffic diverted to other hospitals

The hospital is still working to restore its systems, and it says patients should not trust the hackers' offer.

text:
Facebook had almost 500 million users in June 2010, and its founder was on stage being asked about the privacy backlash. It got so uncomfortable that he had to take his hoodie off.

Kara Swisher asks it straight in the footage. Does he feel he's violating people's privacy.

Mark Zuckerberg answers with history instead. The dorm room, the move to California, and the huge offers to buy the company that he turned down.

"If I knew what I know now, I hope I wouldn't have made those mistakes." He can't change the past, he says.

Then the specific question. What is instant personalization, the feature that had just started passing profiles to partner sites, and what's in it for users.

That's when the hoodie comes off. Printed inside it is the company mission, making the world more open and connected.

The feature was switched on for everyone by default. Anyone who never opened their settings was sharing without having said yes.

That's still the rule worth keeping. The default an app ships with is the deal most people accept, and the real terms live on the settings page.

text:
Messi's Ballon d'Or list is all over the timeline this morning. Barcelona, PSG, Inter Miami. Eight of them across three clubs, and people are calling it crazy.

Fair enough. It is.

But I keep thinking about the one Ballon d'Or I'd swap all eight for. The one that came the year a man missed the biggest night of his life.

Summer 2001. Zidane leaves for Madrid and Juve spend the money on a blond Czech from Lazio who runs like his shorts are on fire. Nobody's sure. You don't replace Zidane. You just hope the hole doesn't swallow the season.

Pavel didn't try to be Zidane. He just ran. Left foot, right foot, didn't matter. He'd shoot from thirty yards like the goal had insulted his family. He'd track back to his own box, then turn up in theirs a few seconds later, still angry. Two Scudetti in his first two years.

Then May 2003. Real Madrid at the Delle Alpi, Champions League semi-final. Figo, Raúl, Ronaldo, Zidane himself. We win 3-1. Nedvěd scores the third. The place goes mad.
A few minutes later he slides in on Steve McManaman and gets a yellow. His second of the competition.
Suspended for the final.

I still remember him after that card. He knew straight away. You could see it on his face. Old Trafford, the final he'd dragged us to, and he'd be watching it in a suit.

We lost it on penalties to Milan. 0-0. Plenty of people still think it goes differently with him on the pitch. I'm one of them. I'll be one of them until I die.

That December he won the Ballon d'Or. Ahead of Thierry Henry. Ahead of Maldini, who'd lifted the trophy he couldn't play for. Nobody in Turin argued.

Then 2006. Calciopoli. Serie B. Stars leaving the building in a queue. Pavel, a Ballon d'Or winner, stayed. Went to Rimini and Crotone and Arezzo with the same face he took to the Bernabéu. Got us back up in one season and kept going until 2009.

That's the bit nobody puts on a graphic. You can win a Ballon d'Or at three clubs. He won his at one, and then chose that one when it had nothing left to offer him except a second division fixture list.

This week we're eighth after Genoa, two goals down and the coach apologising. I'm not saying a 30-yard screamer fixes that. I'm saying I miss watching someone play like losing was a personal problem.

Messi's eight are a record. Pavel's one cost him a final and he'd still do it all again.

Fino alla fine.
